raw_response:
I think about this year's cotton same way I always do. Last year I got about 260 jin of lint per mu, that's good enough, so I will do mostly the same things.

For seed, I buy the Bt cotton seed from the dealer in town, the one that resists bollworm. Everyone around here uses it now, the old varieties nobody plants anymore because the worms eat them. Costs more but saves on spray money.

For fertilizer, before planting I put down compound fertilizer, the 15-15-15 kind, about 2 bags per mu — that's 100 jin, so 50 kg. Then when the cotton starts squaring and flowering in June-July, I topdress urea, maybe 30 jin per mu, that's 15 kg. That gives me good nitrogen. My land here on the plain is not too bad, not too poor. Last year I did this and the bolls came out well.

Counting it up: the compound gives me about 7.5 kg N, the urea gives me about 7 kg N, total around 14-15 kg pure N per mu. Phosphorus about 7-8 kg, potassium about 7-8 kg. I know because the dealer explains the numbers on the bag.

Irrigation — I have my well, thank heavens. I water before planting to get the seedbed wet, then once at squaring, once at flowering, once at boll-filling if the sky doesn't rain. Usually 3 or 4 times total. This year looks dry so probably 4.

Pesticide — cotton is the hungriest crop for spray. Even with Bt seed I still spray for aphids, spider mites, plant bugs. I spray maybe 6 or 7 times through the season. Cannot skip, one bad infestation and the harvest is finished.

Tillage — I plough after last year's stalks come out, then rotary before planting. I use plough to turn the soil deep, it helps the roots go down.

10.1 mu is not small not big, but it's only me and the wife, so we manage with some hired help at picking time.
